description: Calculate X% of a number, what percent one number is of another, a percentage increase or decrease, and the price after a discount. Free, runs in your browser.

formula: X% of Y = Y × X ÷ 100. X is (X ÷ Y × 100)% of Y. Change = (new − old) ÷ |old| × 100. Price after discount = price × (1 − discount ÷ 100).
faq: How do I calculate a percentage increase?
Use “Percentage increase or decrease”: enter the old value as From and the new value as To. A positive result is an increase and a negative one is a decrease.
Why can’t the old value be 0?
A percentage change from 0 is undefined, because it would mean dividing by zero.
Is a percentage the same as percentage points?
No. Going from 10% to 12% is a rise of 2 percentage points, but a 20% increase in the rate. This tool gives the second figure when you enter 10 and 12 as From and To.
good: Results are rounded to two decimals for display. Decimal separators follow your browser’s language settings.
limits: Handles four common percentage questions. It does not do compound percentages over several periods (see the Compound Interest Calculator) or reverse percentages such as “the price before a 20% discount”.

formula: Gross = net × (1 + rate ÷ 100). Net = gross ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100). VAT = gross − net.

name: Loan & Mortgage Calculator
title: Loan & Mortgage Payment Calculator | ToolsKit
description: Estimate the monthly payment, total interest and total repayment for a fixed-rate loan or mortgage. An estimate, not financial advice.

formula: r = annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100; n = years × 12; payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n). At a 0% rate, payment = P ÷ n.
faq: What does it leave out?
Fees, insurance, taxes, variable rates and early repayments. It assumes a fixed rate and equal monthly payments.
Is this financial advice?
No. Results are estimates. Your lender’s figures are the ones that count.
good: Try different terms to see how total interest changes.
limits: Assumes a fixed rate and equal monthly payments. It does not include fees, insurance, taxes, variable rates or overpayments.
disclaimer: Actual rates, fees, insurance, taxes and lender terms vary, and this result is not a loan offer. This tool does not provide financial advice.

name: Compound Interest Calculator
title: Compound Interest Calculator — Free | ToolsKit
description: Project savings growth with compound interest and regular contributions. Shows the formula and assumptions; an estimate, not a forecast.
card: Project growth with regular contributions.
lead: Project how savings grow with compound interest and regular contributions.
steps: Enter the initial amount, contribution, rate, frequency and period.
Results update as you type. Reset starts again.
formula: growth = (1 + r/n)^(n × years); final value = initial × growth + contribution × (growth − 1) ÷ (r/n), where r is the annual rate and n the periods per year.
faq: When are contributions made?
The calculator assumes one contribution at the end of each compounding period, so contribution frequency matches compounding frequency.
Is this a forecast?
No. Real returns vary and are not guaranteed.
good: Results are estimates, not predictions.
limits: Assumes a constant rate and one contribution per compounding period. It does not model fees, taxes or inflation.
disclaimer: Real returns vary and are not guaranteed, and fees, taxes and inflation are not included. This tool does not provide financial advice.
